title: Hardware
intro: Hardware means the physical parts of a computer that you can touch. Learn what each part does and why it is important.

items.name: Monitor
items.info: Displays text, pictures, videos and the computer interface.
items.tip: Clean the screen with a soft, dry or suitable screen-cleaning cloth.

items.name: Keyboard
items.info: An input device used to type letters, numbers, commands and shortcuts.
items.tip: Keep food and liquids away from the keys.

items.name: Mouse
items.info: Controls the pointer and helps you click, select, drag and scroll.
items.tip: Use the scroll wheel to move through long pages.

items.name: CPU Cabinet
items.info: The cabinet or case protects and holds the main internal computer components.
items.tip: Do not open the cabinet while the power is connected.

items.name: Processor (CPU)
items.info: The CPU executes instructions and performs calculations for programs.
items.tip: CPU performance can be described using clock speed and core count.

items.name: Motherboard
items.info: The main circuit board that connects the processor, RAM, storage and other components.
items.tip: Handle the motherboard carefully and avoid static electricity.

items.name: RAM
items.info: Temporary working memory used by programs while the computer is running.
items.tip: More RAM can help when several programs are open at the same time.

items.name: Hard Disk (HDD)
items.info: A storage device that keeps files and programs even after the computer is turned off.
items.tip: HDDs contain moving parts, so avoid shocks while they are operating.

items.name: SSD
items.info: Fast storage that uses flash memory and has no moving disk inside.
items.tip: An SSD can make Windows and applications start faster.

items.name: Power Supply (SMPS)
items.info: Converts and supplies the required electrical power to computer components.
items.tip: Use a reliable power source and do not open a power supply unit.

items.name: Graphics Card
items.info: Processes graphics and sends visual output to a display. Some computers use integrated graphics instead.
items.tip: Keep the graphics card and its cooling system free from dust.

items.name: Cooling Fan
items.info: Moves air to help remove heat from the processor, cabinet and other components.
items.tip: Blocked vents can increase temperature.

items.name: Printer
items.info: Produces a physical copy of digital documents or images.
items.tip: Check paper and ink or toner before printing.

items.name: Webcam
items.info: Captures video for meetings, classes and other applications.
items.tip: Check the privacy settings of apps that use the camera.

items.name: Microphone
items.info: Captures sound and converts it into an electronic signal for the computer.
items.tip: Check the correct microphone input in sound settings.

items.name: Speakers
items.info: Play sound from music, videos, meetings and applications.
items.tip: Adjust volume before playing loud audio.

items.name: UPS
items.info: Provides temporary backup power and can help protect a computer from some power problems.
items.tip: A UPS gives you time to save work and shut down safely during an outage.

items.name: Pen Drive
items.info: A portable USB storage device used to transfer files between computers.
items.tip: Use the safe eject option before removing it.

items.name: Wi-Fi Adapter
items.info: Allows a computer to connect to a wireless network when supported by the adapter.
items.tip: Check drivers if the wireless device is not detected.

items.name: Ethernet Network Card
items.info: Provides a wired network connection using an Ethernet cable.
items.tip: A wired connection is often useful for stable local networking.

title: Software
intro: Software is a collection of programs and instructions that tell the computer what to do.
items: Windows is an operating system used to manage the computer, hardware, files and applications.
MS Word is used to create and format documents such as letters, assignments and notices.
MS Excel is used for tables, calculations, lists, formulas and basic data analysis.
PowerPoint is used to create presentations with slides, text, pictures and diagrams.
A web browser is used to open websites and web applications on the internet.
File Explorer is used to create, copy, move, rename and organize files and folders.
MS Paint is a simple drawing and image-editing application.
Antivirus and security tools help protect a computer from malicious software.
Notepad is a simple text editor useful for plain text notes and basic files.
A PDF reader is used to open and read PDF documents.

title: MS Paint
intro: Paint is a simple program for drawing, colouring and basic image editing.
items: Click Start, type Paint and press Enter.
Choose Pencil, Brush or another drawing tool.
Select a colour from the colour controls.
Hold the left mouse button and move the pointer to draw.
Use Eraser to remove unwanted parts.
Use Ctrl + Z to undo a recent action.
Use Fill to colour a closed area.
Use Select, Crop or Resize when you need to edit an image.
Press Ctrl + S to save your work.

title: MS Word
intro: Word is used to create documents such as letters, assignments, reports and notices.
items: Click Start, type Word and press Enter.
Choose Blank document.
Type your content using the keyboard.
Select text by dragging the mouse over it.
Use the Home tab to change font, size and text colour.
Use Bold, Italic and Underline to format selected text.
Use alignment tools to position text.
Insert pictures or tables when required.
Press Ctrl + S to save and Ctrl + P to print.

title: Shortcut Keys
intro: Keyboard shortcuts can make common computer tasks faster. Hold the first key and then press the second key.
